Research / biology

Somatic evolution & cancer

Understanding cancer through evolutionary dynamics and clonal selection

All research↗

Overview

Cancer is fundamentally an evolutionary process occurring within the body. Our research applies evolutionary theory to understand tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, and treatment resistance. By viewing cancer through an evolutionary lens, we develop new strategies for prediction and intervention.

Questions we explore.

01

Clonal Evolution

Tracking the emergence and competition of cancer cell lineages within tumors using phylogenetic reconstruction

02

Mutation Accumulation

Modeling the temporal dynamics of somatic mutations and their fitness effects in cancer development

03

Treatment Resistance

Understanding how evolutionary processes drive resistance to chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy

04

Tumor Heterogeneity

Characterizing spatial and temporal variation in tumor cell populations and its clinical implications

05

Metastatic Evolution

Investigating the evolutionary trajectories that enable cancer cells to colonize distant sites

Methods & perspective.

We integrate genomic data from single-cell sequencing, bulk tumor samples, and liquid biopsies with mathematical models of evolutionary dynamics. Our approaches include population genetics theory, stochastic simulation, and machine learning to predict tumor evolution and treatment outcomes.

Research directions

Adaptive Therapy Design

Developing evolution-informed treatment strategies that exploit competitive interactions between resistant and sensitive cancer cells

Early Detection Biomarkers

Identifying evolutionary signatures in circulating tumor DNA for early cancer detection and monitoring

Tumor Ecosystem Dynamics

Modeling interactions between cancer cells, immune cells, and the tumor microenvironment as an evolving ecosystem
